transcript.text: Hi everyone. Before we can lock the policy and enable the new event-telemetry pipeline in production, I need to follow the go-live checklist. That means I need the security owner to confirm that the data-handling requirements are met — specifically around the 100 percent sampling, 30-day retention, and raw event payload storage called out in the current draft. I also need the platform finance owner to confirm that the operating-cost requirements are covered. Once I have both confirmations, I can make the binding decision on whether we proceed. Could the security and platform finance owners weigh in?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a cost issue before we proceed. While reconciling the platform invoice ten minutes ago, I found that the production payload volume is expected to cost four times the draft estimate. The approved operating budget only supports exactly 25 percent sampling and exactly 14 days of retention, and a cost alert must be enabled. I have not yet updated the cost worksheet to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a data-handling issue before we proceed. During an unrelated privacy review this morning, I confirmed that the production events contain the fields tax_id and bank_account in three event types. The approved data-handling rule requires both of those fields to be redacted before storage, requires raw payload storage to be disabled, and requires production telemetry to remain enabled once those controls are applied. I have not yet filed this finding in the launch ticket.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: To summarize the blockers from my side: the current draft policy does not meet the approved data-handling rule. Raw payload storage must be disabled, and tax_id and bank_account must be redacted before storage across the three affected event types. Once those controls are applied, production telemetry should remain enabled. I'll file the finding in the launch ticket now so it's tracked. Maya, I cannot confirm the data-handling requirements are met as the draft currently stands.
